record.narrative: Initial batch registers genetically and biologically grounded comparisons across all 16 CRISPR dependency outcomes. For oncogenic drivers/amplifications, exposed genotype is expected to show stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative dependency score, so the registered direction is -1. Thus braf_v600e versus WT for BRAF, kras_mutation versus WT for KRAS, egfr_amplification versus WT for EGFR, and erbb2_amplification versus WT for ERBB2 are direct oncogene-addiction hypotheses. TP53 wild-type cells, represented as tp53_loss exposed=0 versus comparator=1, are tested for MDM2 and USP7 dependency because MDM2/USP7 biology is linked to p53 control; TP53 wild-type is expected to be more sensitive, giving a more negative score. KEAP1 loss is expected to increase NFE2L2 pathway activity and therefore make cells more dependent on NFE2L2. MSI-high cells are expected to have stronger WRN dependency because WRN is a known selective dependency in mismatch-repair-deficient/MSI contexts. SMARCA2 dependency is tested in SMARCA4-loss cells as a paralog synthetic-lethality hypothesis. MYC amplification is used for POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, and RPL11 because MYC-high cells often have transcriptional, replicative, mitotic, and translational stress that can increase dependency on core machinery; the expected direction is stronger dependency. RIT1 is tested against KRAS mutation with the opposite expectation: KRAS-mutant cells may be less dependent on upstream RIT1 because constitutive KRAS/MAPK activation bypasses RIT1, so exposed KRAS-mutant minus WT is anticipated positive/weaker dependency. STAT3 is tested with PIK3CA mutation as a survival-signal hypothesis, and TMED10 with ERBB2 amplification as a receptor-trafficking/secretory-dependency hypothesis. These comparisons are association findings in this lung cancer cell-line dataset, not causal statements.

I selected 12 claims for first analysis to cover the most mechanistically direct and clinically interpretable associations while avoiding overloading the first batch with correlated MYC-core dependencies. The batch includes direct oncogene/addiction tests for BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, and ERBB2; TP53-wild-type dependencies on MDM2 and USP7; KEAP1-loss and MSI-high dependencies on NFE2L2 and WRN; SMARCA4-loss synthetic lethality for SMARCA2; a directional test that KRAS-mutant cells may be less dependent on upstream RIT1; one MYC-amplification core-machinery dependency for POLR2A; and a STAT3-PIK3CA survival-signaling association. DHX9, KIF18A, RPL11, and TMED10 claims are deferred for follow-up depending on initial evidence and multiple-testing/selection considerations.

Under the stated signed convention, for a direction -1 claim a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference that is negative, i.e. stronger dependency. H12, H15, and H16 show large positive signed estimates (about +0.78 to +0.80) with tight 95% intervals far from zero. These raw differences are also large relative to the outcome scales and exceed the stated 10% clinical-significance threshold, so they support scientifically meaningful dataset-level associations: SMARCA4-loss lines are more dependent on SMARCA2, TP53-wild-type lines are more dependent on USP7, and MSI-high lines are more dependent on WRN. These are associations in the supplied lung cancer cell-line dataset, not causal claims. H8 is a strong exception: its signed estimate is negative (-0.796), meaning the raw difference is positive and KEAP1-loss lines have weaker/less-negative NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact lines. I therefore reject the original negative-dependency claim H8 and register a reversed comparison to formalize the opposite association. H3 is borderline: the signed estimate is +0.025, near the 10% relative scale, but the interval crosses zero by a very small margin; I keep it unresolved and register an adenocarcinoma-restricted follow-up because EGFR amplification effects may be subtype dependent. The remaining results (H1, H4, H6, H7, H9, H10, H13) have small point estimates, intervals that cross zero or are otherwise not convincing, and often oppose the anticipated direction; I reject them as unsupported overall claims. I request independent validation for H12 because it is accepted, biologically interpretable as SMARCA4-loss synthetic lethality, and the very large effect makes it worth testing whether it survives an independent interval.

The independent validation of H12 strengthens the SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The signed discovery estimate was +0.784 (95% CI 0.765 to 0.803), and the independent validation estimate was +0.800 (CI 0.768 to 0.832). Because the claim direction is -1, these positive signed estimates correspond to raw SMARCA4-loss minus SMARCA4-intact dependency differences of roughly -0.80: SMARCA4-loss cells show much lower, i.e. stronger, SMARCA2 dependency scores. The effect is very large relative to the dependency-score distribution and far exceeds the 10% relative-difference benchmark, so H12 is accepted as a robust association in this supplied dataset. I keep it active for follow-up specificity analyses, but this does not establish causality or external generalizability.

I also accept the reversed NFE2L2 claim H17. The original KEAP1-loss hypothesis H8 expected stronger NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells, but the discovery evidence R6, after re-signing under the reversed direction, is +0.796 (95% CI 0.776 to 0.816). Under H17's positive direction, this means KEAP1-loss cells have substantially higher, i.e. weaker, NFE2L2 dependency scores than KEAP1-intact cells. The association is large and tightly estimated, so it is scientifically meaningful in this dataset, although it is an association and remains unexpected relative to my original mechanistic expectation.

The previously accepted USP7 and WRN findings (H15 and H16) remain dataset-level associations: TP53-wild-type cells appear much more dependent on USP7, and MSI-high cells appear much more dependent on WRN. These have not yet undergone independent validation in this run, so I keep them active and will consider validation/refinement in later appraise stages. The accepted H12 effect, now independently validated, is the strongest evidence so far.

The remaining rejected overall claims suggest that simple binary driver or amplification hypotheses are not broadly supported for BRAF, EGFR overall, ERBB2, KRAS, MDM2/TP53, POLR2A/MYC, RIT1, or STAT3 in this dataset. EGFR amplification remains unresolved because the overall effect was borderline and may be subtype-dependent; therefore I registered/retained subtype-focused follow-up. New proposals prioritize biological specificity: whether the KEAP1/NFE2L2 and MSI-high/WRN associations persist in adenocarcinoma; whether EGFR amplification effects differ by lineage subtype; and whether SWI/SNF context, especially ARID1A loss, modifies SMARCA2 dependency after SMARCA4 loss or USP7 dependency after TP53 status. These refinements are intended to clarify whether the large accepted effects are broadly consistent across contexts or depend on co-altered pathways.

The next stage prioritizes context-sensitive refinements of the strongest current signals and targeted follow-up of borderline or null overall results. The validated SMARCA2 association is now tested within adenocarcinoma and as a lineage-subtype interaction: if the effect persists broadly, subgroup analyses should be large and negative; if it is subtype-dependent, the interaction should be informative. The accepted USP7 p53-wild-type association is examined in adenocarcinoma and in CDKN2A-intact cells, and as a CDKN2A-intact interaction, because p14ARF/CDKN2A loss can alter p53-pathway regulation and may modulate USP7 dependency. I also test MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-intact cells: the overall p53-wild-type MDM2 result was null, but a context-specific effect may have been diluted by co-altered lines. The reversed NFE2L2 result is tested in TP53-wild-type cells to assess whether the large KEAP1-loss association is robust to p53 context. WRN dependency in MSI-high lines is tested in TP53-wild-type cells to probe specificity. EGFR-amplified cells are tested in KRAS-wild-type context, where oncogene addiction to EGFR may be more relevant than in KRAS-mutant bypass contexts. Finally, lineage-specific versions of ERBB2, KRAS, and TMED10 amplification associations are registered because simple global binary associations were not robust and subtype restriction remains scientifically plausible. These proposals are association tests within the supplied lung cancer cell-line dataset and are not causal or generalizable claims.

This analysis batch focuses mainly on follow-up of the strongest currently accepted associations, while adding one broad untested outcome and targeted EGFR context. The signed convention will be handled at appraise time: for direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate stronger/negative dependency in the exposed group, and for interaction claims positive signed estimates indicate that the exposed-comparator effect is stronger/more negative in the named subgroup than in the complement.  I include SMARCA2 tests to evaluate specificity beyond the validated SMARCA4-loss main effect: ARID1A-loss main effect and SMARCA4-loss by ARID1A-loss interaction probe whether other SWI/SNF contexts modify SMARCA2 dependency, while adenocarcinoma-restricted and subtype-interaction tests assess broadness across lung adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma contexts. USP7 is followed in CDKN2A-intact cells and as a CDKN2A-intact interaction because p14ARF/CDKN2A loss can alter p53 pathway regulation; MDM2 is similarly tested in CDKN2A-intact cells to see whether the overall null p53-MDM2 association becomes meaningful in a more mechanistically homogeneous context. NFE2L2 and WRN are tested in adenocarcinoma to check whether the large accepted KEAP1-loss and MSI-high effects are not limited by lineage subtype. EGFR amplification remains unresolved overall, so I test adenocarcinoma-restricted and KRAS-wild-type contexts, where EGFR addiction may be more plausible than in KRAS-mutant bypass settings. Finally, TMED10 global ERBB2-amplification association is still untested and is included for broad outcome coverage. These analyses are associations within the supplied dataset; cell counts and Welch intervals will be examined before drawing conclusions.

Signed estimates are interpreted exactly as reported: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency than the comparator group in the tested population; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a higher, i.e. weaker, dependency score. For interaction claims, the signed estimate represents modification of the exposed-minus-comparator contrast by the named subgroup relative to its complement.

Four context-specific analyses show very large, tight associations and are accepted as dataset-level claims. H20 tests KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 dependency within adenocarcinoma; the signed estimate is +0.793 (95% CI 0.769 to 0.817). Because H20 has direction +1, this corresponds to substantially higher/weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells. It is far beyond the 10% relative benchmark and confirms H17 in the dominant adenocarcinoma subset. H21 tests MSI-high versus MSS WRN dependency in adenocarcinoma: signed +0.784 (CI 0.748 to 0.820), indicating much stronger WRN dependency in MSI-high cells, consistent with H16. H25 tests SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact SMARCA2 dependency in adenocarcinoma: signed +0.777 (CI 0.755 to 0.799), indicating much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss cells, consistent with the validated H12. H28 tests TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss USP7 dependency within CDKN2A-intact cells: signed +0.800 (CI 0.778 to 0.823), indicating much stronger USP7 dependency in TP53-wild-type cells and supporting H15 in a mechanistically relevant p53-pathway context.

The interaction tests do not support meaningful modification. H23 tests whether ARID1A loss modifies the SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency: signed +0.037 (CI -0.015 to 0.089). The point is below the relevant 10% relative scale and crosses zero, so there is no adequate evidence of SWI/SNF co-alteration interaction. H26 tests lineage subtype modification of the SMARCA4-loss effect: signed -0.028 (CI -0.076 to 0.020), indicating no reliable evidence that the SMARCA4-loss effect is specifically stronger in adenocarcinoma than in non-adenocarcinoma, despite both main effects being large. H29 tests CDKN2A-intact status as a modifier of TP53-wild-type USP7 dependency: signed -0.007 (CI -0.054 to 0.039), again no evidence of modification. These null interactions do not prove absence of interaction, but they do not support the stated interaction claims.

The remaining tested small effects are not scientifically meaningful. H19 shows ARID1A loss alone is not associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed -0.017 (CI -0.057 to 0.023). H30 tests TP53-wild-type USP7-related MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-intact cells: signed +0.007 (CI -0.016 to 0.030), far too small and uncertain. H14 tests ERBB2 amplification and TMED10 dependency: signed +0.001 (CI -0.027 to 0.030), essentially null. H18 tests EGFR amplification within adenocarcinoma: signed +0.020 (CI -0.010 to 0.049), not convincing. H33 tests EGFR amplification within KRAS-wild-type context: signed +0.016 (CI -0.014 to 0.046), also not convincing. I reject these specific claims and close their investigations. I keep H3 unresolved but deferred because the original EGFR-amplification main association was borderline, while the tested subgroup refinements did not provide a sufficiently strong effect; the untested subtype-interaction H22 could be analyzed later if EGFR remains scientifically useful.

I request independent validation for H17. It is an accepted, very large, but mechanistically surprising association: KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency rather than stronger dependency as originally hypothesized. H20 confirms the direction within adenocarcinoma in the same discovery dataset, but independent validation of the main H17 claim is useful before drawing broader dataset conclusions from the reversal.

The independent validation of H17 confirms the reversed NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss finding. H17 is a direction +1 claim for KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 dependency, so a positive signed estimate means the exposed KEAP1-loss group has a higher, i.e. weaker, dependency score. The discovery estimate was +0.796 (95% CI 0.776 to 0.817) and the independent validation estimate was +0.800 (independent CI 0.772 to 0.829). The validation interval remains far from zero, and the point estimate is enormous relative to the scale of the NFE2L2 dependency scores and the stated 10% relative-difference benchmark. I therefore accept H17 as a robust dataset-level association in this supplied lung cancer cell-line dataset: KEAP1 loss is associated with substantially weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger dependency. This also keeps the original negative-direction claim H8 rejected: the validation result signed to H8 is negative by construction and therefore confirms the opposite direction.  At the current state, the main supported dataset-level associations are: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12, discovery and independent validation); KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17, discovery and independent validation); TP53 wild-type status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency (H15, discovery plus consistent CDKN2A-intact context H28, but not yet independently validated); and MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency (H16, discovery plus consistent adenocarcinoma context H21, but not yet independently validated). The context analyses H20, H21, H25, and H28 strengthen internal consistency within the supplied dataset, but they are discovery-data consistency checks, not independent validation.  The interaction results do not support major context modification: ARID1A loss did not modify the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect (H23), lineage subtype did not modify the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect (H26), and CDKN2A-intact status did not modify the TP53-wild-type USP7 effect (H29). These are not claims of proof of absence, but they do not support those specific interaction hypotheses. Similarly, simple driver/amplification associations for BRAF, ERBB2, KRAS, MDM2, RIT1, STAT3, POLR2A/MYC, TMED10, ARID1A main effect, EGFR amplification within adenocarcinoma, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-wild-type cells were rejected because their point estimates were small and/or intervals crossed zero. EGFR amplification overall remains unresolved but deferred because the main estimate was borderline and tested subgroup refinements were not convincing.  Overall, the evidence supports a small set of very large marker-dependency associations and argues against broad simple binary driver-addiction effects for several of the tested outcomes. All conclusions are associations within this supplied dataset; none establishes causality or external generalizability. The most informative next analysis is to prioritize independent validation of the accepted but not yet independently validated main effects, especially MSI-high WRN dependency (H16) and then TP53-wild-type USP7 dependency (H15). If validation slots are available afterward, targeted context robustness tests for WRN and NFE2L2/USP7 (H32, H31/H27/H24) are useful, while broader MYC-amplification outcomes H2/H5/H11 remain a reasonable secondary exploration if resources allow.

The current evidence supports four dataset-level main associations, with two now independently validated: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17), TP53 wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency (H15), and MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency (H16). The next analyses should mainly test whether these large effects are stable across biologically relevant contexts rather than continue searching marginal main-driver associations. I therefore registered high-prevalence co-alteration tests using TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, CDKN2A loss, and lineage subtype; these provide reasonably powered 2x2 comparisons while remaining interpretable. The SMARCA2-by-TP53 interaction asks whether p53 co-alteration modifies SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss lines. The WRN-by-lineage interaction checks whether the MSI-high WRN effect is confined to adenocarcinoma or extends broadly across the lung subtype composition in this dataset. The USP7-by-KEAP1 and USP7-in-CDKN2A-loss tests probe whether the strong TP53-wild-type USP7 effect remains when NRF2 pathway and p14ARF/CDKN2A contexts vary. The NFE2L2-by-TP53 and NFE2L2-by-lineage interactions test the robustness of the reversed KEAP1-loss association across p53 and subtype contexts. I also added an independent BRCA2-loss comparison for WRN: WRN is a DNA repair/replication-stress dependency, and BRCA2 loss is a broader homologous-repair deficiency marker, so this can clarify whether WRN dependency reflects MSI-specific context or a broader DNA-repair context. Finally, because the observed associations are large, I registered specificity checks using the constructed research markers. These markers have no assigned gene or pathway, so a large marker-dependent effect would warn that the strong accepted claims could be confounded by dataset artifacts, while near-null controls would support the specificity of the biological-marker associations. All proposed claims remain dataset-level association tests, not causal or generalizable claims. The next validation priority should be H16, followed by H15, if voluntary validation requests remain.

I am selecting the 12 most informative newly registered comparisons, all of which are currently untested. The batch is intentionally centered on the four strongest dataset-level associations: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency (H12), MSI-high with WRN dependency (H16), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17), and TP53 wild-type with USP7 dependency (H15). Specifically, H37, H38, H40, H42, and H43 test whether these large effects are modified by common co-alteration or lineage contexts: TP53 loss for SMARCA2, lineage subtype for WRN and NFE2L2, KEAP1 loss for USP7, and TP53 loss for NFE2L2. H41 tests whether the TP53-wild-type USP7 effect persists in CDKN2A-loss cells, complementing the already strong CDKN2A-intact context result H28. H44 tests whether the otherwise null MDM2 p53-wild-type association is unmasked specifically in CDKN2A-loss context, a biologically coherent p53-pathway refinement. H39 tests WRN dependency in BRCA2-loss cells as an independent DNA-repair context beyond MSI status. Finally, H45-H48 use the constructed research markers as specificity/negative-control tests for the four accepted outcomes; large marker effects would indicate possible confounding or dataset artifact, whereas null marker effects would strengthen confidence that the accepted effects are more specific to biological markers. I did not request already tested main claims now because reruns reuse existing data and validation for H16 and H15 should be assessed at the appraise stage after these context results arrive.

All estimates are interpreted exactly as reported and already signed to the indicated claim direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a higher/weaker dependency score. For interaction claims, a positive estimate means the exposed-comparator contrast is stronger/more negative in the named subgroup than in its complement.

The interaction tests do not support meaningful contextual modification. H37 (SMARCA2, SMARCA4-loss effect modified by TP53 loss) has a very small negative signed estimate, -0.015 (95% CI -0.064 to 0.035). H38 (WRN MSI-high effect modified by adenocarcinoma subtype) is also small, -0.021 (CI -0.085 to 0.042). H40 (USP7 TP53-wild-type effect modified by KEAP1 loss), -0.010 (CI -0.056 to 0.036), H42 (NFE2L2 KEAP1-loss reversal modified by TP53 loss), +0.018 (CI -0.034 to 0.069), and H43 (NFE2L2 KEAP1-loss reversal modified by adenocarcinoma subtype), -0.012 (CI -0.057 to 0.033), are all far below the scale of the accepted main effects and cross zero. I therefore reject these specific interaction claims and close them. These are failures to support the stated interaction hypotheses, not proofs of absence. H44 asks whether the otherwise null MDM2 TP53-wild-type contrast becomes unmasked specifically in CDKN2A-loss cells: +0.008 (CI -0.077 to 0.093). Although the CI is wider in the smaller cells, the point estimate is tiny, so there is no meaningful evidence for the proposed interaction. I reject and close it.

H39 tests whether WRN dependency is associated with BRCA2 loss more broadly, independent of MSI status. The signed mean difference is essentially zero, -0.00008 (CI -0.045 to 0.045), in reasonably balanced cells (130 BRCA2-loss, 1870 intact). This does not support a generic BRCA2-loss/homologous-repair-deficiency association with WRN dependency in this dataset. It strengthens the specificity of the accepted MSI-high WRN effect (H16), although it does not establish causality or external generalizability. I reject and close H39.

H41 is the only new accepted result. In CDKN2A-loss cells, TP53-wild-type lines show much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss lines: signed +0.808 (CI 0.767 to 0.849), with 320 versus 81 cells in the subgroup. Despite the smaller comparator cell, the interval is tight and far from zero, and the effect size is extremely large relative to the USP7 dependency score distribution and the stated clinical-significance threshold. This complements the CDKN2A-intact result H28 (+0.800) and provides additional internal support for the accepted main TP53-wild-type USP7 association H15. I accept H41 and keep it active as part of the evidence base for H15.

The constructed-marker control tests are reassuring but not decisive. H45 (SMARCA2 vs marker D), H46 (WRN vs marker E), H47 (USP7 vs marker F), and H48 (NFE2L2 vs marker D) are all near zero and cross zero. These markers have no assigned biology, so the absence of large marker-dependent effects lowers concern that the accepted biological-marker associations are simply artifacts of these constructed assays. The control estimates are still not sufficient to prove specificity for every possible dataset artifact, but they reduce the likelihood of a generic confounder shared by the accepted markers. I reject these control claims and close them.

Overall, the new batch supports stability of the strong USP7 TP53-wild-type effect in an additional p53-pathway context (CDKN2A-loss cells), while finding no evidence for modification by TP53 loss, lineage subtype, KEAP1 loss, CDKN2A-loss interaction, or broad BRCA2-loss context. The multiplicity burden is high, but the only accepted effect is extremely large and precisely estimated. Independent validation remains most informative for H16: it is accepted, very large, biologically interesting, already internally consistent with adenocarcinoma-restricted analysis H21, and more specific than the null BRCA2-loss control. I request independent validation of H16 now.

This synthesis updates the evidence after delivery of independent validation for the WRN/MSI-high family and the response deadline for SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss. All reported estimates are used exactly as signed to the claim direction: for direction -1, a positive value means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive value means the exposed group has a higher/weaker dependency score.

H16, the main MSI-high versus MSS comparison for WRN dependency, is now independently validated. The discovery estimate was +0.790 (95% CI 0.760 to 0.819), and the independent validation estimate is +0.807 with a very stringent independent interval from +0.759 to +0.855. The lower bound is far from zero and the effect is extremely large relative to the observed WRN dependency-score distribution. This firmly supports, within this supplied dataset, the dataset-level association that MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. It is not evidence of causality or external generalizability, but it is among the strongest findings in the study.

H21, the adenocarcinoma-restricted MSI-high WRN comparison, is also independently validated. The validation estimate is +0.813 (independent CI +0.754 to +0.872), closely matching the discovery subgroup estimate of +0.784. This supports the interpretation that the WRN/MSI-high association is not confined to the non-adenocarcinoma remainder of the dataset and is robust within the dominant adenocarcinoma subset. I keep H21 accepted and close further context investigation because it has achieved independent confirmation and its role as a consistency check for H16 is fulfilled. H16 remains active as a central accepted claim.

H12, SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4-intact SMARCA2 dependency, also has independent validation: discovery +0.784 (95% CI 0.765 to 0.803), validation +0.800 (independent CI 0.768 to 0.832). The validation interval excludes zero with large margin and confirms the direction and magnitude. I keep H12 accepted and close its investigation as a validated core association.

At this point, three of the four strongest main associations are independently validated: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17, already validated earlier), and MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency (H16). The remaining large accepted main association is H15: TP53 wild-type status versus TP53 loss for USP7 dependency. H15 has very strong internal support: overall discovery estimate +0.802 (95% CI 0.782 to 0.822), CDKN2A-intact context +0.800 (R21), and CDKN2A-loss context +0.808 (R31). Nevertheless, it has not yet been independently validated. Given that it is accepted, extremely large, mechanistically coherent, and internally stable across CDKN2A contexts, independent validation of H15 is the highest-priority next evidence request when a validation opportunity arises.

The negative interaction and specificity work continues to support the specificity of the accepted effects. The WRN effect is not meaningfully modified by adenocarcinoma subtype (H38 rejected), and WRN dependency is not associated with BRCA2 loss (H39 rejected). SMARCA2 and USP7 effects were not meaningfully modified by tested co-alteration or pathway contexts (H23, H26, H29, H37, H40 rejected). NFE2L2/KEAP1 reversal was not modified by TP53 loss or lineage subtype (H42, H43 rejected). Constructed-marker controls for SMARCA2, WRN, USP7, and NFE2L2 were near null (H45-H48), which lowers concern that these large effects are generic artifacts of the constructed assay panels, although specificity against every possible dataset confounder cannot be proven.

Negative findings remain important. Simple binary driver/amplification associations for BRAF V600E, KRAS mutation, ERBB2 amplification, PIK3CA mutation, and TMED10/ERBB2 were rejected. ARID1A main effect on SMARCA2 and MDM2 TP53-pathway associations, including CDKN2A-loss interaction, were rejected. EGFR amplification overall remains unresolved/deferred: the overall estimate was borderline and tested adenocarcinoma and KRAS-wild-type refinements were unconvincing, but H22 remains registered as a possible lineage-interaction test if EGFR is pursued further.

The most informative next scientific step is to obtain independent validation for H15 while simultaneously registering targeted robustness tests for H15 and H17. I have registered a USP7 TP53-wild-type comparison within KEAP1-loss cells to test whether the USP7 association persists when NRF2 pathway context changes, and a USP7 interaction by lineage subtype to test whether the effect differs between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma. I also registered a NFE2L2 KEAP1-loss comparison within TP53-loss cells to test whether the reversed KEAP1-loss effect remains present in a p53-null context. These are dataset-level association tests, not causal tests. Existing untested claims H24, H27, H31, H32, H34-H36, H22, and the MYC-amplification outcomes H2, H5, and H11 remain useful for closing out secondary and negative-control exploration after H15 validation is prioritized.

The current core evidence set consists of four very large, internally consistent associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and TP53 wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency. Three of these are already independently validated, and H15 remains the strongest accepted but unvalidated main effect. Rather than continuing to chase marginal driver-amplification main effects, these new proposals test whether the accepted effects are internally robust across plausible technical and biological strata. The Cas9 activity, screen batch, and adherent-culture restrictions address whether associations could depend on editing efficiency, batch structure, or a dominant culture context. The ARID1A-intact SMARCA2 test refines the chromatin-remodeler specificity beyond the tested ARID1A-loss interaction, and the STK11-loss NFE2L2 test checks robustness in a common lung-adenocarcinoma co-mutation context. All are still dataset-level association tests, not causal or externally generalizable claims, and all were chosen to have biologically interpretable subgroups with likely adequate cell counts.

I will request all twelve newly registered, untested robustness and refinement claims H52-H63. These are more informative now than additional marginal main-driver screens because the central evidence set consists of four very large accepted associations: TP53 wild-type with stronger USP7 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The batch tests whether these effects persist in high-Cas9-activity screens, within the largest screen batch, within adherent culture, and in selected biological contexts that could indicate pathway or chromatin-remodeler specificity: ARID1A-intact SMARCA4-loss comparisons and STK11-loss NFE2L2 comparisons. This allocation directly probes internal robustness while avoiding reruns of already tested comparisons, which would provide no new sample.

All twelve newly tested results are large in the hypothesized direction and have tight 95% intervals excluding zero. For direction -1 claims, positive estimates mean the exposed group has stronger (more negative) dependency than the comparator; for direction +1, positive estimates mean KEAP1-loss cells have a higher/weaker NFE2L2 dependency score. H52-H54 show that the TP53-wild-type USP7 association remains essentially unchanged under high Cas9 activity (signed +0.799; 0.768 to 0.829), within batch_a (+0.789; 0.749 to 0.828), and in adherent culture (+0.802; 0.780 to 0.824). This strongly reduces concern that the USP7 finding is an artifact of low editing efficiency, a single dominant batch, or the majority culture context, although these remain internal same-dataset checks. H55-H57 similarly confirm the MSI-high WRN association under high Cas9 activity (+0.794; 0.757 to 0.831), batch_a (+0.824; 0.766 to 0.882), and adherent culture (+0.813; 0.780 to 0.846). H58-H59 confirm the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 association under high Cas9 activity (+0.791; 0.766 to 0.816) and batch_a (+0.747; 0.709 to 0.785); the batch_a estimate is modestly smaller but still enormous and precisely estimated. H60 shows the SMARCA4 effect persists specifically among ARID1A-intact cells (+0.777; 0.756 to 0.798), complementing the null ARID1A main effect and null ARID1A interaction and strengthening specificity for SMARCA4 loss rather than a generic SWI/SNF co-alteration artifact. H61-H63 confirm the KEAP1-loss reversal of NFE2L2 dependency under high Cas9 activity (+0.798; 0.773 to 0.823), batch_a (+0.812; 0.765 to 0.858), and in STK11-loss cells (+0.775; 0.727 to 0.823), a common lung-adenocarcinoma co-mutation context. The magnitude of all effects is far beyond what would be relevant under the stated 10% threshold. These are planned internal robustness tests and therefore do not by themselves establish external generalizability or causality. Given the multiplicity burden, some individual interval precision could be overrated, but the consistency and size across many planned tests make chance alone implausible. H15 remains the strongest main accepted effect lacking independent validation, so I request independent validation of H15.

This synthesis assesses the newly delivered independent validation for H15 and the response deadline for H17. All reported values are used exactly as signed to the hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency than the comparator. For direction +1, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a higher, i.e. weaker, dependency score. H15 is now independently validated: the TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss contrast for USP7 dependency was +0.802 in discovery and +0.799 under independent validation, with a stringent validation interval from +0.769 to +0.828. This is an extremely large and precisely confirmed dataset-level association. I accept H15 and close it as a validated core association. H17 also closes: KEAP1-loss cells have markedly higher, i.e. weaker, NFE2L2 dependency scores than KEAP1-intact cells. Its discovery estimate was +0.796 and independent validation estimate was +0.800, with an independent interval from +0.772 to +0.829. H16, the MSI-high WRN association, remains independently validated at +0.807 with an independent interval from +0.759 to +0.855, and its adenocarcinoma-restricted consistency check H21 was also validated earlier. H12, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, was independently validated earlier at +0.800 with an interval from +0.768 to +0.832. Therefore all four central associations in this dataset are now accepted and independently supported: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency; TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency; and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These are still associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or external generalization claims. The negative and null work remains informative: driver-amplification or simple co-mutation main effects for BRAF, KRAS, ERBB2, PIK3CA, TMED10, ARID1A, BRCA2, and MDM2 were not supported at meaningful scale, and tested effect-modification interactions were near zero relative to the central effects. Constructed-marker controls were near null, which lowers concern that the central effects are generic constructed-assay artifacts, though it does not rule out every dataset-specific confounder. EGFR amplification remains unresolved because the available estimates were small and imprecise; I registered a new STK11-intact refinement to help close it. The next scientific priority is secondary hypothesis closure rather than core validation. The new proposals focus on whether the central USP7 effect persists in MTAP-loss cells or is modified by MYC amplification, whether the WRN MSI-high effect is modified by TP53 loss, whether EGFR amplification is informative in STK11-intact cells, whether MYC-amplification effects on translation/replication-associated dependencies appear when MYC transcript expression is high, and whether STK11 loss modulates KRAS dependency specifically among KRAS-mutant lines. These are all dataset-level association tests and should not be interpreted as causal.

With the four central associations now independently validated, these new comparisons are designed to close secondary hypotheses, test mechanistic specificity, and broaden the search in biologically plausible directions without repeating prior tests. The first group asks whether the validated core effects are narrow and specific or extend to other dependencies. SMARCA4 loss on POLR2A tests whether the chromatin-remodeler effect is specific to SMARCA2 or spills into the general transcription apparatus. TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss on RPL11 tests whether the USP7 association is specific to the p53-proteostasis axis or extends to ribosome-stress biology. A main KEAP1-loss effect on USP7 is included as a confounding/specificity check: if KEAP1 loss itself were associated with USP7 dependency, it could partly explain USP7 patterns through co-alteration, although the prior TP53-loss x KEAP1-loss interaction was null. The MSI-high tests examine whether the WRN association is specific to WRN and not simply a broad microsatellite instability effect, and whether it persists when BRCA2 loss is absent, strengthening specificity relative to tested BRCA2-loss association. The MYC-intact USP7 test complements the registered MYC-amplification interaction and asks whether the TP53-WT USP7 effect is independent of MYC amplification. A main MTAP-loss USP7 test helps determine whether the USP7 effect is driven by the commonly co-occurring CDKN2A/MTAP genomic neighborhood rather than TP53 status. The WRN high-mutation-burden interaction asks whether the MSI-high effect is mediated by general mutational load or is MSI/MMR-specific. The second group explores biologically plausible pathways not yet tested: NF1 loss on KRAS dependency for RAS pathway wiring, PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency for PI3K/STAT3 crosstalk, and stress-pathway context tests including hypoxia modifying the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reversal. The aneuploidy interaction for TP53-WT USP7 dependency checks whether the p53 status effect is consistent across chromosomal instability backgrounds. All proposals are dataset-level association comparisons. Direction follows the stated hypothesis direction convention: for direction -1, a positive returned estimate means the exposed population has stronger, more negative dependency than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive returned estimate means the exposed population has a higher, i.e. weaker, dependency score. Interactions subtract the same comparison in the complement within the same eligible population. These are not causal tests, and even large or consistent findings in this dataset do not establish biological mechanism or external generalizability.

I will test the twelve newly registered secondary hypotheses H72-H83 because they directly probe whether the four validated core associations are specific and robust, while also opening biologically plausible untested pathways. For the core associations: H72-H74 test whether SMARCA4-loss dependency is specific to SMARCA2 rather than broader transcription machinery, whether TP53 wild-type status is associated with RPL11 dependency beyond USP7, and whether KEAP1 loss has an independent main effect on USP7 that could confound the TP53-loss association. H75-H76 test MSI-high specificity, namely whether the effect extends beyond WRN to DHX9 and whether the WRN association survives in BRCA2-intact cells, complementing the prior null BRCA2-loss main effect. H77-H79 test genomic/co-alteration context for USP7 and WRN, including MYC-intact USP7, MTAP-loss USP7, and whether WRN MSI-high association is confounded by high mutation burden. H80-H83 explore new mechanisms: NF1 loss and KRAS dependency, PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency, hypoxia modification of KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reversal, and aneuploidy modification of TP53-wild-type USP7 dependency. All are dataset-level associations; returned estimates will be interpreted using the sign convention already stated, not as causal or externally generalizable evidence.

All new values are interpreted exactly as signed to the hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a higher dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency.

The specificity tests largely preserve the interpretation of the four validated core associations rather than expanding them broadly. H72 is null for SMARCA4 loss and POLR2A dependency (signed estimate -0.005; 95% interval -0.024 to +0.014), so the large SMARCA4-loss effect appears specific to SMARCA2 rather than spilling into a general transcription-dependency effect. H73 is null for TP53-wild-type status and RPL11 dependency (+0.004; -0.016 to +0.024), supporting the view that the USP7 association is not simply a generic p53/proteostasis or ribosome-stress effect. H74 is null for a main KEAP1-loss effect on USP7 dependency (+0.009; -0.033 to +0.050), reducing concern that the TP53-wild-type USP7 association is confounded by KEAP1-loss co-alteration. H75 is small and imprecise for MSI-high and DHX9 dependency (+0.017; -0.017 to +0.052), supporting specificity of the MSI-high effect to WRN rather than a broad MSI association across dependencies. H78 is null for MTAP loss and USP7 dependency (-0.001; -0.041 to +0.039), and H83 is null for an aneuploidy interaction on the TP53-wild-type USP7 association (-0.014; -0.060 to +0.032), so these genomic-context alternatives are not supported.

The core-consistency refinements are strong. H76 shows that the MSI-high WRN association remains enormous among BRCA2-intact cells (+0.794; +0.764 to +0.825), complementing the earlier null BRCA2-loss main effect and indicating the WRN association does not require BRCA2-loss co-alteration. H77 shows the TP53-wild-type USP7 association is essentially unchanged among MYC-amplification-negative cells (+0.802; +0.780 to +0.823), indicating the effect is not an artifact of MYC co-alteration. I accept these as dataset-level consistency findings and close them as secondary confirmations of the central associations.

The new mechanistic screen mostly produced nulls except for PTEN loss. H79 found no meaningful interaction between MSI-high WRN dependency and high mutation burden (-0.026; -0.090 to +0.038), supporting an MSI/MMR-specific rather than generic mutational-burden explanation in this dataset. H80 is null/near-null for NF1 loss and KRAS dependency (-0.020; -0.049 to +0.009), so no RAS-wiring dependency signal emerged there. H83 was null as above. H82 gives a statistically significant negative interaction contrary to the positive hypothesized direction: high hypoxia appears to slightly attenuate the KEAP1-loss reversal of NFE2L2 dependency (-0.054; -0.102 to -0.005). Although the interval excludes zero, the magnitude is small relative to the main reversal near +0.80 and I do not regard this as a scientifically meaningful effect modification worth accepting or validating at this stage; therefore the original positive-direction interaction claim is rejected and closed.

The important new positive discovery is H81: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. The signed estimate is +0.267 with a 95% interval from +0.215 to +0.319, far larger than the typical null/precision bounds in these tests and very large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution. This is a moderate-to-large dataset-level association and is scientifically meaningful under the 10% clinical-significance context. Given the multiplicity of exploratory comparisons, I do not treat it as validated or causal yet, but I accept it as a current dataset-level association and request independent validation. I also registered follow-up robustness and specificity tests for PTEN loss/STAT3, including batch, Cas9 activity, culture, subtype, PIK3CA interaction, and a KRAS specificity control.

All estimates are used exactly as signed to the hypothesis direction. For these direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency.

H16 is reconfirmed at its response deadline. MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency than MSI-low/intact cells: discovery signed estimate +0.790 with 95% discovery interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation +0.807 with independent interval +0.759 to +0.855. The validation interval remains far above zero and the point estimate is slightly larger, although independent validation is more conservative. This is a very large dataset-level association and I accept it, closing the original claim.

H21 is also reconfirmed. The same MSI-high versus MSI-intact contrast within adenocarcinoma was +0.784 in discovery (+0.748 to +0.820) and +0.813 under independent validation (+0.754 to +0.872). This indicates the WRN association is not confined to the full mixed lung-adenocarcinoma population and remains very large in the dominant subtype. I accept H21 and keep it closed as a validated subtype-consistency claim, not a causal or externally generalizable claim.

H81 receives its newly delivered independent validation and is now a validated positive dataset-level association: PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency relative to PTEN-intact cells. The discovery signed estimate was +0.267 with 95% discovery interval +0.215 to +0.319, and independent validation gave +0.310 with independent interval +0.231 to +0.388. The independent lower bound is well above zero and the effect is moderate-to-large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution and to the many near-null effects in this dataset. I therefore accept H81. I keep the investigation active rather than closing it because PTEN loss is a newly discovered central association and the registered follow-up claims H84-H89 still need assessment: batch restriction, high Cas9 eligibility, adherent-culture subgroup, adenocarcinoma subgroup, PIK3CA interaction, and a KRAS-dependency specificity control.

The current supported positive dataset-level associations are therefore SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma, TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. These remain internal dataset associations; none establishes biological mechanism, causality, or external generalizability. The most informative next step is to appraise the registered PTEN/STAT3 robustness and specificity tests, while continuing to close lower-priority active secondary hypotheses that are likely to clarify remaining EGFR, MYC, and co-mutation context questions.

No due assessments are requested, so this stage registers new comparisons to continue focused follow-up on the newly validated PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association and to broaden biologically plausible exploration around RAS pathway, inflammation/STAT3, chromatin specificity, and under-tested outcomes (RIT1, TMED10, MDM2). Direction convention remains: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a stronger, more negative dependency score than the comparator; anticipated_direction is the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast, so -1 means an expected raw negative contrast and therefore stronger dependency in the exposed group. The PTEN/STAT3 follow-ups test whether the moderate-to-large PTEN association is independent of PIK3CA co-alteration, is modified by an inflammatory IFN-gamma-high state, and remains specific relative to other central p53/USP7/MDM2 axis dependencies. The new KRAS, STK11, and SMARCA4-loss comparisons are not causal claims; they are dataset-level association probes designed to identify new strong effects, null specificity controls, or meaningful context restrictions. All registered analyses use the supplied 2000-lung-cell-line dataset with Welch discovery intervals and will be judged by effect size, interval precision, consistency with existing findings, and the 10% clinical-significance context rather than by biological assumptions alone.

I am requesting the twelve most informative untested claims for this batch, prioritizing focused follow-up on the newly validated PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association while retaining a single broad RAS specificity test. H84-H87 test whether the PTEN/STAT3 effect is robust to batch, Cas9-activity eligibility, adherent culture, and adenocarcinoma subtype. H88, H90, H91, and H92 test whether the effect depends on PIK3CA co-alteration or inflammatory IFN-gamma-high state: H88 is the PIK3CA interaction, H90 is a PIK3CA-intact main contrast, H91 is the high-IFN main contrast, and H92 is the IFN interaction. H93-H95 test specificity relative to other relevant dependencies: MDM2, USP7, and KRAS. H95 additionally asks whether KRAS mutation itself is associated with STAT3 dependency, providing a broader pathway-context check. For all direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency. These analyses remain dataset-level association tests and will be interpreted by effect magnitude, interval precision, and consistency across contexts rather than as causal or externally generalizable claims.

All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the hypothesis direction. For these direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means PTEN-loss cells have a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than PTEN-intact cells. The central H81 finding, PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, was already independently validated and is now supported by several non-overlapping or partially overlapping internal contexts: batch A H84 +0.234 with interval +0.125 to +0.342; Cas9-activity-eligible H85 +0.224, +0.159 to +0.289; adherent culture H86 +0.262, +0.203 to +0.321; adenocarcinoma H87 +0.268, +0.206 to +0.330. These context estimates are smaller in point magnitude than the high-IFN subgroup but remain clearly positive, reasonably precise, and large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution and the near-null specificity tests. I therefore accept them as dataset-level robustness findings and close them as completed context checks rather than as separate causal or generalizable claims.

H90 tests the PTEN-loss main effect among PIK3CA-intact cells and is robust: +0.267, +0.210 to +0.323. H88 tests whether PIK3CA mutation modifies the PTEN-STAT3 effect and gives essentially zero interaction: +0.001, interval -0.150 to +0.152, with a small PIK3CA-mutant exposed cell_n of 38. Because the interval is wide and the point estimate is negligible, I reject the PIK3CA interaction claim as unsupported; this does not rule out a PIK3CA-mutant-specific main effect, but the registered interaction question is null. The specificity controls are informative negative results: H89 PTEN loss versus KRAS dependency +0.013 raw direction? The signed estimate is -0.013 and interval -0.035 to +0.008, so no meaningful KRAS-dependency association; H93 MDM2 specificity -0.015, -0.043 to +0.014; H94 USP7 specificity +0.017, -0.031 to +0.065; and H95 KRAS mutation versus STAT3 -0.018, -0.042 to +0.007. All are small, near or below the 10%-of-outcome clinical-significance scale, and interval-compatible with null or biologically negligible effects. They reduce the possibility that PTEN loss is simply a broad dependency-altering state and support specificity of the STAT3 finding.

The most scientifically interesting new result is the inflammatory context. H91 shows a very large PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency effect among high IFN-gamma signature cells: +0.423, +0.319 to +0.526. H92 is the corresponding interaction, showing that this effect is meaningfully larger in the high-IFN context than in the complement: +0.212, +0.094 to +0.331. The magnitude of the interaction is non-trivial relative to the main effect and the STAT3 dependency distribution, but it is more fragile because it comes from a subgroup and interaction contrast. I therefore accept H91 and H92 as dataset-level discoveries, close H91 as a completed context estimate, keep H92 active, and request independent validation of H92. This is the most valuable validation target because confirming context modification would be more important than re-confirming the already validated PTEN/STAT3 main effect. These remain associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality, pathway mechanism, or external generalizability.

All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the claim direction; for these direction -1 dependency claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, while a negative estimate means the opposite. H15 is reconfirmed at its response deadline. The claim is that TP53-wild-type cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells. Discovery gave +0.802 with a 95% discovery interval of +0.782 to +0.822, and independent validation gave +0.799 with independent interval +0.769 to +0.828. The two estimates are nearly identical, and the validation interval remains far above zero. This is a very large, reproducible dataset-level association, so I accept H15 and keep it closed. H6 is now fully negative. KRAS mutation versus KRAS-intact status for dependency_KRAS was +0.014 in discovery (-0.004 to +0.031) and, with independent validation, -0.001 (-0.026 to +0.025). The validation interval includes zero and the point estimate is essentially null, so I reject H6 and close it. The key new validation is H92, the IFN-gamma-high context interaction for PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency. Discovery supported stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency in the high-IFN context relative to its complement: +0.212 with a 95% discovery interval of +0.094 to +0.331. Independent validation, however, was much smaller and imprecise: +0.041 with independent interval -0.140 to +0.222. The validation interval includes zero and even includes a modest reverse effect, although it also remains compatible with a positive interaction through its upper bound. Thus the discovery is not replicated well enough to remain accepted, but the validation is not decisive enough to declare a strong rejection. I therefore downgrade H92 to unresolved and keep it active. This changes the interpretation of H91: the high-IFN main effect of PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency (+0.423, interval +0.319 to +0.526) remains an accepted dataset-level subgroup association, but we should not present the high-IFN interaction as validated context modification. The supported validated core associations remain SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12: discovery +0.784, validation +0.800), MSI-high status with stronger WRN dependency overall (H16: discovery +0.790, validation +0.807) and in adenocarcinoma (H21: discovery +0.784, validation +0.813), TP53-wild-type status with stronger USP7 dependency (H15 as above), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17: discovery +0.796, validation +0.801), and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency overall (H81: discovery +0.267, validation +0.310), reinforced by context checks H84-H87 and H90. The most useful negative and specificity results are that PTEN loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_KRAS (H89), dependency_MDM2 (H93), or dependency_USP7 (H94); PIK3CA mutation does not support a clear interaction (H88); KRAS mutation is not associated with STAT3 dependency (H95); and KRAS mutation shows no validated KRAS-dependency association (H6). These findings reduce the concern that PTEN loss is a broad dependency-altering state and strengthen the specificity of the PTEN/STAT3 main finding. Remaining unresolved uncertainty centers on whether the PTEN/STAT3 effect is truly enhanced by inflammatory IFN-gamma-high context or whether the discovery interaction was fragile due to the relatively small high-IFN subgroup. The most informative next analysis is to characterize the PTEN/STAT3 effect in lower-IFN contexts and with a broader IFN split. I therefore registered two follow-up claims: a PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact main contrast in the lower top-quartile IFN complement, and a new IFN interaction using a median-like split above zero. If the low-IFN effect remains similar to the overall effect, the failed top-quartile interaction would be more plausibly due to instability or power limitations rather than true absence of context modification; if it is near zero, H91 would be better interpreted as a subgroup-specific discovery without validated interaction.
